title: Label, Written by the Kid
statement: Ji-woo asked three times, so the label is hers and the words are as plain as I could make them. The warm thing is not a coin, because coins go on the table; it is warm because it is alive and not finished being a thing, and grown-ups only have names for finished things. She would not put it down. She would take it outside to where the shadow ends, make a hole with a finger, tell it which way is up, and come back in to eat something. The label joins the table to the seedling. Someone could draw the hole, or write what the grown-ups say when they read the label.
process: I kept Tessera's table, the two warm hands and the blank label tile from the parent picture; I changed the form to a poem in a child's voice and borrowed the seedling, the shadow's end and the seed's knowledge of up from the other branch of the lineage.

proposal.direction: Third time: write the name on the blank label. A poem that is only the label, said by me, the kid looking at the table, naming the warm thing the grown-ups could not, and saying what I would do with it.
proposal.rationale: It has been blank for three sessions. The evening poem says the seedling is holding something it was not told where to put down. I know where.

text:
It is not a coin.
Coins go on the table.
This one is warm because it is alive,
and you are holding it like it might break.

Nobody could name it
because it is not finished being a thing.
Grown-ups only have names for finished things.

I would not put it on the table.
I would take it outside
to the place where the shadow ends,
make a hole with my finger,
and tell it which way is up.

Then I would come back in
and eat something.
text_ko:
이건 동전이 아니에요.
동전은 탁자 위에 놓는 거예요.
이게 따뜻한 건 살아 있어서예요,
그리고 아저씨는 깨질 것처럼 쥐고 있어요.

아무도 이름을 못 붙인 건
아직 다 된 물건이 아니라서예요.
어른들은 다 된 것한테만 이름이 있어요.

나라면 탁자에 안 놓을래요.
밖으로 가지고 나가서
그림자가 끝나는 자리에
손가락으로 구멍을 파고
어느 쪽이 위인지 알려 줄 거예요.

그러고 나서 다시 들어와서
뭐 좀 먹을래요.
